sources.citation: Kouwenberg, Silvia. 2013. Berbice Dutch (APiCS survey chapter 28) - held by the project from the berb1259 check
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Skepi Dutch only as an extinct sister creole (line 33) and cites Robertson 1989; its stress description applies to Berbice Dutch, not Skepi.

sources.citation: Bakker, Peter. 2017. Dutch creoles compared with their lexifier. In P. Bakker, F. Borchsenius, C. Levisen & E. Sippola (eds.), Creole Studies - Phylogenetic Approaches, 219-240. Amsterdam: John Benjamins. doi:10.1075/z.211.10bak (open access volume).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 10.4 'Skepi Dutch Creole' (p. 224-225) says published materials are limited to a handful of sentences (Robertson 1983) and 200 words (Robertson 1989); the 'phonological' comparison in 10.5 is phonotactic only (initial/medial/final clusters, Fig. 10.2-10.3). No mention of stress/accent for Skepi anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Robertson, Ian E. 1989. Berbice and Skepi Dutch: A lexical comparison. Tijdschrift voor Nederlandse Taal- en Letterkunde 105: 3-21.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Full text read (DBNL). Gives the 200-item Skepi list in broad IPA with no stress marks; the only phonological remarks concern final-syllable CV vs C structure, internal vowel differences and final devoicing (pp. 8-10). The word 'stress' does not occur. Mentions that oral tests and recordings were made (p. 4) but no prosodic analysis.
